items.title: EMA recommends authorisation of Rasonque for metastatic pancreatic cancer
items.summary: EMA’s human medicines committee (CHMP) has recommended granting a marketing authorisation in the European Union for Rasonque (daraxonrasib), an oral treatment for adults with…

items.title: Geron’s Rytelo stumbles in phase 3 as Novartis gears up for post-JAK inhibitor blood cancer bid
items.summary: Geron has discontinued a phase 3 trial of its Rytelo in JAK inhibitor-pretreated myelofibrosis after an independent data monitoring committee ruled that the study was unlikely to succeed, just as Novartis is gearing up for a delayed FDA approval bid for its pelabresib.

items.title: After GSK's Q3 approval spate, Hibsago preps for 'concentrated' US hep B launch
items.summary: Armed with a trio of recent high-profile approvals, GSK is banking on its specialty medicines to drive its next wave of growth, even as investor enthusiasm cooled Wednesday morning amid reports of restructuring charges and a vaccine sales dip at the British drugmaker.

items.title: Amgen hit with FDA warning letter for ‘misleading’ Vectibix promotion
items.summary: Amgen has been handed an FDA warning letter over a video promoting its cancer drug Vectibix, but the company said that the issues stemmed from an “inadvertent” submission and was not made available publicly.

items.title: AMA and EMA issue joint guidance on Ebola vaccine development
items.summary: EMA’s Emergency Task Force (ETF) and the African Medicines Agency (AMA) have published a joint position paper to support the timely start of clinical trials for potential…

items.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
items.summary: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027.…

items.title: Ascletis’ challenger to Lilly’s Foundayo hits goals in phase 2 diabetes trial
items.summary: A phase 2 trial of Ascletis’ oral GLP-1 drug candidate has hit its primary and secondary endpoints, positioning the Chinese biotech to mount a two-front attack on Eli Lilly’s Foundayo.

items.title: Genmab's $8B Merus bet delivers as bispecific combo halves risk of death in phase 3
items.summary: Capping off a busy few days in Spain, Genmab reported results from the first interim analysis of a phase 3 trial showing that adding its bispecific antibody petosemtamab to Merck & Co.'s Keytruda cut the risk of death by 50% compared with Keytruda alone in patients with PD-L1-positive recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

items.title: FDA’s rare disease framework aims to ‘stand the test of time’
items.summary: During a public hearing Wednesday to discuss a newly proposed rare disease framework, FDA center director Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., said the agency aims to design a scheme that “stands the test of time.”

items.title: Lilly’s retatrutide bests Ozempic on blood sugar, weight loss in phase 3 diabetes showdown
items.summary: Eli Lilly’s triple-G drug candidate retatrutide has beaten Novo’s Ozempic in a head-to-head phase 3 trial, driving deeper reductions in blood sugar and body weight across the 80-week study.

items.title: Regulatory tracker: Sun's Ilumya wins FDA expansion; Bayer's FXIa inhibitor gets world-1st nod in China
items.summary: In this tracker, Fierce Pharma is recording the regulatory progress of in-market products, including expansions into key geographies and new indications. Some of these updates may not meet the bar for standalone stories, but we think they are still worth mentioning.

items.title: Pfizer looks to reroute supply after flooding sidelined India injectables plant
items.summary: A Pfizer joint venture with Zydus Cadila in India that manufactures sterile injectables, including chemotherapy drugs for U.S. cancer patients, remains closed after severe flooding in July, with the company estimating that new supplies could begin returning in mid-to-late 2028 under a best-case scenario.

items.title: Jazz's $820M Actio buyout gives rise to Setara, armed with $90M series A
items.summary: Setara Biosciences, a privately held spinout formed following Jazz Pharmaceuticals' acquisition of Actio Biosciences in September, has raised $90 million in series A financing to advance its clinical-stage neuroscience drug candidate and earlier-stage pipeline.

items.title: Sanofi considering ‘moonshot’ treatments as M&A targets to survive Dupixent patent cliff
items.summary: Sanofi is considering “moonshot” treatments among the potential acquisition targets needed for the French pharma to urgently replenish its pipeline, Chief Financial Officer François-Xavier Roger told Fierce.

items.title: BioMarin inks up to $475M deal to challenge Fabry ERT incumbents
items.summary: BioMarin is paying $70 million upfront to license a Fabry disease drug candidate, expanding the franchise it acquired through its $4.8 billion takeover of Amicus Therapeutics.

items.title: Blue Matter ‘turbocharges’ global reach of comms agency Cognite with acquisition
items.summary: The deal stands to "turbocharge" Cognite's global reach and growth opportunities, chief business officer Sean Cush pointed out.

items.title: Eversana combines forces with UK-based AI health economics research firm Estima in acquisition
items.summary: Estima's AI and automation capabilities for health economics and outcomes research will help Eversana further leverage the "technology-first solutions" infused into its platform.

items.title: Gilead reveals partial clinical hold on 2 CAR-T cell therapy trials
items.summary: Gilead Sciences announced on its third-quarter earnings call Oct. 29 that the company has placed a partial clinical hold on two studies for the CAR-T cell therapy KITE-753 in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL).

items.title: When drug development gets personal
items.summary: When Third Rock Ventures partner Jigar Raythatha was diagnosed with brain cancer, he found himself relying on a drug originally developed by Agios, a biotech his firm backed years before he joined. On "The Top Line," he shares how the experience changed his perspective on drug development.

items.title: Chutes & Ladders—Lilly unifies global markets as 36-year vet Patrik Jonsson retires
items.summary: Lilly will unite its U.S. and international commercial units as a long-time exec retires. Enanta's CEO will hang up his hat after 23 year at the helm. Estrella has tapped a new a CEO to lead it through a clinical trial.

items.title: Bracco invests $230M in first US diagnostic imaging manufacturing facility
items.summary: Bracco announced it will invest $230 million to establish its first U.S. manufacturing facility for injectable contrast media in Sanford, North Carolina.

items.title: AstraZeneca cuts early-phase prostate cancer pipeline
items.summary: AstraZeneca has punted a pair of early-phase prostate cancer programs as part of its quarterly pipeline clear out.

items.title: Bambusa shoots past IPO targets as Aspen trims offering
items.summary: Bambusa Therapeutics has upsized its IPO, selling more shares at the midpoint of its target range to gross $168.9 million for bispecific R&D. But Aspen Neuroscience underperformed expectations, hitting the bottom end of its target range and selling slightly fewer shares than expected.

items.title: Roche launches differential diagnosis test for mesothelioma
items.summary: Roche announced the global launch of its VENTANA BAP1 (SP527) test, an automated, ready-to-use immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay.

items.title: Molecular Partners to lay off up to 44% of workforce in radiotherapy pivot
items.summary: Molecular Partners plans to lay off up to 44% of its staff as it focuses its declining cash reserves on a radiotherapeutic pipeline led by an early-phase small cell lung cancer drug candidate.

items.title: Eli Lilly scraps phase 2 Alzheimer's program after drug falls short of expectations
items.summary: Eli Lilly has dropped its phase 2 Alzheimer's disease program for mevidalen, marking another setback for the experimental drug as the Big Pharma expands its neuroscience pipeline through multibillion-dollar acquisitions.

items.title: Merck outlines 2027 as ‘another year of investment’ despite recent clinical wins
items.summary: Even as a wave of clinical trial wins bolsters its momentum, Merck & Co. is prioritizing ongoing pipeline and commercial expansions over near-term margin growth, hoping to strengthen its long-term prospects past Keytruda's loss of exclusivity.

items.title: BMS walks away from $80M neurodegeneration bet after phase 1
items.summary: Bristol Myers Squibb has scrapped a phase 1 program it bet $80 million on just two years ago.

items.title: Flagship brings 3 biotech platforms together to launch AI drug discovery player Etcelera
items.summary: Flagship Pioneering unveiled Etcelera today, a new AI-powered biotech emerging from stealth that aims to predict how potential medicines will act in patients.

items.title: Oura, UC San Diego Health collaborate to study GLP-1 outcomes using continuous smart ring data
items.summary: Oura is pushing further into clinical healthcare research with its first clinical trial to study the link between smart ring data and obesity-treatment outcomes.

items.title: Why researchers may have found the biological culprit behind Angelman syndrome
items.summary: Scientists have known for a while that Angelman syndrome is caused by the loss of a specific gene, but they didn't understand how this gene loss leads to the failure of brain development in infants with the disease.

items.title: Biogen CEO tells analysts he’s focused on early-stage R&D as ‘we were not very good with that’
items.summary: Biogen's CEO has pointed to the company's ability to take five drugs into clinical trials so far this year as evidence of its new focus on early-stage R&D.

items.title: ‘The patient need is enormous’: Syntax programs stem cells into pancreatic beta cells in 4 days
items.summary: Chicago-based Syntax Bio believes it has cracked the code for turning stem cells into pancreatic beta cells in as little as four days.

items.title: GSK predicts ‘some limited impact’ to UK roles as restructuring rolls on
items.summary: GSK’s global restructuring plan is likely to see “some limited impact” to roles on the Big Pharma’s home turf of the U.K., executives have confirmed.

items.title: As Skyrizi and Rinvoq dominate AbbVie's Q3, analysts ask what's next
items.summary: Analysts were eager to learn more about AbbVie's plans beyond immunology as Rinvoq and Skyrizi headlined the Chicago drugmaker's third-quarter earnings.
